references.text: Earlier in the same chapter it is mentioned that six cities shall be cities of refuge, which verse 13 confirms the number of.
The following verses explain the distribution of the six cities of refuge: three on the east side of the Jordan and three in the land of Canaan.
Moses set apart three cities of refuge on the east side of the Jordan: Bezer, Ramoth, and Golan.
Repeats the law concerning cities of refuge and the command to set aside three cities in the promised land.
Mentions the possibility of adding three more cities to the original three, making a total of six cities of refuge.
Joshua carries out the Lord's command to appoint cities of refuge, and the six cities are named.
Hebron is given to the descendants of Aaron as a city of refuge for someone who has killed another unintentionally.
Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim is mentioned as a city of refuge.
Golan in Bashan is mentioned as a city of refuge for the descendants of Gershon.
Kedesh in Galilee is mentioned as a city of refuge.
Bezer is mentioned as a city of refuge for the tribe of Reuben.
Ramoth in Gilead is mentioned as a city of refuge for the tribe of Gad.
The basic law concerning a place of refuge for someone who kills without intent, which the cities of refuge are based on.
